stories.title: Watch Mode: Continuous File Monitoring
stories.content:
Developer runs 'memo' or 'memo watch' in project root. memo loads config, acquires exclusive lock, checks for updates, scans all files (unless --skip-scan), then enters fsnotify watch loop. On file changes, debounces for 30s (configurable), batches files, and sends to AI for analysis. Results are validated against JSON schemas (retry up to 5x on failure), then written to .memo/index/*.json.

Happy path:
1. main.go: cmd.Execute()
2. cmd/root.go: rootCmd dispatches to watchCmd (default)
3. cmd/watch.go: runWatch() acquires lock via analyzer.TryLock()
4. cmd/common.go: initIndex() creates .memo/index with empty JSON files
5. cmd/config.go: LoadConfig() reads config.yaml with defaults
6. analyzer/banner.go: PrintBanner() shows ASCII art, version, greeting
7. analyzer/watcher.go: NewWatcher() creates fsnotify watcher
8. analyzer/watcher.go: ScanAll() adds non-ignored files to pending
9. analyzer/watcher.go: Flush() calls onChange with pending files
10. analyzer/analyser.go: Analyse() batches files, processes with AI
11. analyzer/validator.go: ValidateIndex() checks JSON schemas
12. analyzer/watcher.go: Run() enters fsnotify loop for changes

stories.title: Scan Mode: One-shot Analysis
stories.content:
Developer runs 'memo scan' for CI or manual one-time analysis. Same setup as watch mode but immediately flushes pending files and exits after completion. Useful for generating fresh index without staying resident.

Happy path:
1. cmd/scan.go: runScan() same setup as watch
2. analyzer/watcher.go: ScanAll() collects all files
3. analyzer/watcher.go: Flush() triggers immediate analysis
4. analyzer/analyser.go: Analyse() processes all files in batches
5. Exit after completion

stories.title: MCP Mode: Agent Index Queries
stories.content:
AI agent runs 'memo mcp' via MCP integration. Server reads JSON-RPC requests from stdin, responds on stdout. Two tools available: memo_list_keys to navigate index structure, memo_get_value to retrieve specific data. Server adds warning if analysis is in progress.

Happy path:
1. cmd/mcp.go: mcpCmd validates .memo/index exists
2. mcp/server.go: Serve() creates server, calls Run()
3. mcp/server.go: Run() reads JSON-RPC from stdin
4. mcp/server.go: handleRequest() dispatches to handlers
5. mcp/query.go: ParsePath() parses [file][key][index] notation
6. mcp/query.go: ListKeys()/GetValue() executes query
7. mcp/server.go: writeResponse() sends result

stories.title: Schema Validation with Retry
stories.content:
After AI generates JSON updates, validator checks output against schemas. If validation fails, formats errors into feedback prompt and retries (up to 5 times) with the error context. This ensures index files always conform to expected structure.

Happy path:
1. analyzer/analyser.go: analyseBatch() calls AI
2. analyzer/validator.go: ValidateIndex() checks schemas
3. On failure: FormatValidationErrors() creates feedback
4. Retry with feedback prompt (max 5 times)
5. Validate until valid or max retries

stories.title: Single Instance Lock
stories.content:
Only one watcher can run per project directory. TryLock uses OS-specific file locking (flock on Unix, LockFileEx on Windows) on .memo/watcher.lock. Includes PID for debugging. Lock released on process exit.

Happy path:
1. cmd/watch.go: runWatch() calls analyzer.TryLock()
2. analyzer/lock_unix.go: Flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)
3. Write PID to lock file
4. Return file handle for deferred Unlock()
5. On conflict: error 'another instance is running'

stories.title: Auto-Update Check
stories.content:
On startup in watch/scan modes, async checks GitHub releases for newer version. 2-second timeout prevents blocking. If update available, shows notice in banner with platform-specific install command.

Happy path:
1. cmd/watch.go: runWatch() calls CheckUpdateAsync()
2. internal/updater.go: goroutine queries GitHub API
3. Compare semver, return UpdateInfo if newer
4. analyzer/banner.go: PrintBanner() shows update notice

stories.title: MCP Path Query Security
stories.content:
MCP query parser has security controls: allowedFiles whitelist (arch/interface/stories/issues), 100-char key limit, control character rejection, no path traversal. Invalid paths return clear error messages.

Happy path:
1. mcp/query.go: ParsePath() extracts file name
2. Validate against allowedFiles whitelist
3. validateKey() checks length and chars
4. Return structured PathSegment array
5. On invalid: return descriptive error
